question: Does a timeout stop an opponent run?
answer: No: after an 8+ pt run, a timeout nets -0.31 pts over the next 2:00 vs playing on (CI -0.40 to -0.23).
findings: Timeout: next 2:00 net +0.51 pts (CI +0.44 to +0.58), n=9313.
No timeout: next 2:00 net +0.83 pts (CI +0.79 to +0.87), n=23790.
Both groups outscore the opponent after the run (mean reversion plus the ball); same-state gap -0.31.
Q4 only: timeout minus none -0.26 pts (CI -0.42 to -0.10), n=6980.
method: Trigger = score making an unanswered run 8+ pts, >= 2:30 left in quarter, margin within 20. Timeout in that dead ball vs no timeout in next 60 s; net points next 120 s; matched on run size and quarter.
data: ESPN play-by-play via sportsdataverse, NBA 2011-12 to 2025-26, 16,242 games, 33,103 runs.
